memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: We took all the towns on the plateau, and all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salekah and Edrei, towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan. (Og king of Bashan was the last of the Rephaites. His bed was decorated with iron and was more than nine cubits long and four cubits wide. It is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.) - Deut 3:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses pauses to note a remarkable detail: Og's iron bed was over nine cubits long — roughly thirteen feet. Og was the last of the Rephaites, a race of giants, and this detail underscores just how imposing he was. His very bed became a museum piece, a lasting reminder of the enormous king Israel had faced. And yet, for all his size and strength, Og had fallen before the Lord. The giant who should have been unbeatable was defeated because God fought for His people.

There is a quiet triumph in this detail. The bed remained as a monument, but Og himself was gone. His impressive size, his iron furnishings, his fortified kingdom — none of it could stand against the power of God. The mightiest human strength is nothing before the Lord.

This speaks to us whenever we feel small against the powers that seem to loom over our lives. Whether it is a personal struggle, a fearful circumstance, or the intimidating powers of our age, we are tempted to measure them against our own strength and despair. But the right measure is God's power, before which even giants fall.

We do not overcome by being bigger or stronger than our giants. We overcome because our God is greater than them all. David faced Goliath not with confidence in his own might but in the name of the Lord of hosts (1 Sam 17:45). And the greatest giants — sin, death, and the devil — have been defeated not by our strength but by Christ, who through His death destroyed the one who held the power of death (Heb 2:14). Whatever giant you face, remember: it is no match for your God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What giant in your life have you been measuring against your own strength?
2. How does God's power over the mightiest foe change your perspective?
3. How does Christ's victory over sin and death encourage you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord of hosts, no giant is a match for You. When intimidating powers loom over me, help me measure them against Your greatness, not my strength, trusting in Christ who defeated the greatest enemies of all. Amen.
